title: Closing praise, self-assessment and goodbye
summary: Allen thanks him and praises his drive; Mitchell says he never satisfied himself, and the tape ends with a photograph request.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, I must thank you again and I'm sure that other people will be hearing some of the... I'll play some of these tapes and that maybe someday we can quote some of these in the publication.

And I know a lot of people will appreciate your advice on how you learned the trumpet and how you play and how those records were made because there have been so many people interested in your work more now than maybe in those days they realized what a great trumpet you were. Oh, well, I've got a long ways to go.
Well, you still played wonderful. I mean, you did what the trumpet's supposed to do. You didn't play like a clarinet but you played like a real cornet.
I... Well, you know, I always liked trumpet and always wanted to learn to play trumpet really well but I never, just never was able to...

Well, I'm sure if Jelly Roll and all those people weren't wrong when they told that you were one of the masters and you played right, maybe you didn't do as much technically as some but you had the right style and really a wonderful drive and spirit on those records that you made that nobody will ever forget those and have heard those.
Yeah, well, I always liked the trumpet but I've never satisfied myself in the way I've played. Well, I know nobody, no real artist has ever really satisfied me.
Well, thank you very much and I'll turn it off now. Well, I want to take your picture if you don't mind. Yeah, look, look, look. And... stuff
